From: Ben Park <ben.park@seoulpantry.example>
To: Miguel Vance <miguel.vance@coastlinecold.example>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 10:00:00 +0000
Subject: [FROZEN LTL] TEST-C8 / PO# SYNC8PO1 / SO# SYNC8SO1 / VERNON,CA - ARLINGTON HEIGHTS,IL 60005

Dear Miguel,

Please send quote for below.

PO# SYNC8PO1
Commodity: Frozen Fish Cake / Frozen Sanukki Udon Noodle
3 Pallet ~ 4,355 lbs
REFER (FROZEN)

Pick up: ColdVault
Requested pick up date: 9/30/26 or 10/1/26

Deliver to: 300 E. Lake Dr., Arlington Heights, IL 60005
Delivery Date: Before or on 10/7/26

Thank you
Ben

questions.question: What's the street address for the ColdVault pickup in Vernon?
What's the consignee name at 300 E. Lake Dr., Arlington Heights?
How many cases are on PO SYNC8PO1?

why: Edge case: a quote request is treated as an order-in-waiting, since a quote needs the same fields and the rate is what's being requested. The pickup is named only as a facility, so origin is filled from the order text alone (company, plus Vernon, CA from the subject line) and the street address is asked rather than pulled from the customer's profile. Of the two pickup dates offered, the earliest is used; 'before or on 10/7' is the delivery deadline. 'REFER (FROZEN)' with no number gets the company's standard frozen range and a flag to confirm. The TMS needs a consignee name, which the order omits, so it is asked, as is the missing case count.
